newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN chief sees imminent Zaire ceasefire - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: UN chief sees imminent Zaire ceasefire - spokesman.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan expects a ceasefire to be agreed in the coming days at peace talks in South Africa between Zaire's government and rebels, his spokesman said on Wednesday.

"We feel that it's probably only a matter of days before a ceasefire is agreed and put into effect," Fred Eckhard told a briefing at the U.N.'s European headquarters in Geneva during a visit by Annan.

The rebels, who have taken more than a quarter of Zairean territory since taking up arms last October to topple ailing ruler President Mobutu Sese Seko, are outside Zaire's second largest city Lubumbashi where they have met resistance from Zairean troops.

Representatives of rebel leader Laurent Kabila and of Mobutu wrapped up four days of talks in South Africa on Tuesday with a statement recognising the need for talks on a peaceful solution and a truce.
Eckhard did not make clear how or when a ceasefire might be reached and implemented.
He said the assessment of Mohamed Sahnoun, representative at the talks of the U.N. and the Organisation of African Unity, was also that a ceasefire "would be a matter of days".
Eckhard also said that the U.N. chief's military assessment was that "most likely, it would not be possible for Kabila to win militarily."
"Taking east Zaire is one thing, taking western Zaire is something else...in terms of the ethnic composition of Zaire, in terms of supplies," he said.
"His (Annan's) argument to Kabila is that if you are convinced that you have the support of the people, then why not go to elections?"
